articles.title: Bhagwandutt S.N.K. High School
articles.subtitle: Bandwar's oldest school — established 1942 as a Sanskrit gurukul
articles.summary: Bhagwandutt S.N.K. High School is the oldest educational institution in Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1942 by Pandit Taradutt Pathak in memory of his father Pandit Bhagwan Dutt Pathak, it began as a free Sanskrit gurukul serving students from across Bihar. Today it operates as a government secondary school (Classes 9-10) under the Bihar Department of Education, holding UDISE code 10201013302. It is one of ten schools in the village, alongside [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]], [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]], and the village's several primary schools.

content.heading: Origins — The 1942 Gurukul
content.text: In 1942, during the final years of British rule, Pandit Taradutt Pathak established a Sanskrit school in memory of his father Pandit Bhagwan Dutt Pathak. It was a traditional gurukul — students came from across Bihar, and education, food, and lodging were all provided free of cost. This was a period when formal schooling was rare in rural Bihar, and the establishment of a free gurukul in a village like Bandwar was an act of considerable ambition. The school's founding predates Indian independence by five years, and it was among the earliest educational institutions in the region.

content.heading: After Independence
content.text: Following India's independence, the school was brought under the Department of Education and became a government secondary school. It continued to serve Bandwar and the surrounding areas of Begusarai for decades. The school's transition from a private gurukul to a government institution mirrored the broader transformation of education in post-independence Bihar — a period in which the state took on the responsibility for schooling that had once been borne by philanthropists and communities.

content.heading: Present Day
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school today serves Classes 9 and 10 with an enrolment of just 12 students — 2 boys and 10 girls. It has 4 teachers, 5 classrooms, a library, and electricity, but no boundary wall and no playground. Like [[gps-paschimibandwar|GPS Paschimibandwar]] and several other schools in the village, the school faces the challenges common to rural secondary education in Bihar — low enrolment, limited infrastructure, and difficulty retaining teachers.

content.heading: Legacy
content.text: The school's history represents both the ambition of Bandwar's founders and the challenges faced by rural secondary education in Bihar. A place that once offered free education to students from across the region now struggles to sustain its enrolment. Students who would once have come to Bandwar for its gurukul now travel to Begusarai, Barauni, or even Patna for their secondary education. And yet the school remains — a quiet witness to the eighty years of educational history that have passed through its gates.

faqs.q: When was S.N.K. High School established?
faqs.a: S.N.K. High School was established in 1942 by Pandit Taradutt Pathak, in memory of his father Pandit Bhagwan Dutt Pathak. It is the oldest educational institution in Bandwar village.

faqs.q: What does 'S.N.K.' stand for?
faqs.a: S.N.K. stands for 'Sanskrit Nagri Kanya' — though in its present form the school is co-educational. The name reflects its origins as a Sanskrit gurukul founded in the memory of Pandit Bhagwan Dutt Pathak.

faqs.q: What is the UDISE code of S.N.K. High School?
faqs.a: The school's UDISE code is 10201013302. It operates under the Bihar Department of Education as a government secondary school serving Classes 9 and 10.

faqs.q: How many students study at S.N.K. High School today?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 12 students — 2 boys and 10 girls — taught by 4 teachers. The low enrolment reflects the wider challenges of rural secondary education in Bihar.

faqs.q: Was S.N.K. High School always a government school?
faqs.a: No — it began in 1942 as a private Sanskrit gurukul, providing free education, food, and lodging to students from across Bihar. After independence, it was brought under the Department of Education and became a government secondary school.

articles.title: UHS +2 Bandwar
articles.subtitle: The village's higher secondary school — Classes 9 to 12
articles.summary: UHS +2 Bandwar (Upgraded High School +2) is the higher secondary school of Bandwar village in Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1955 and holding UDISE code 10201008406, it provides education from Class 9 to Class 12 with a total enrolment of 601 students — the largest school in Bandwar. It is the natural next step for students completing Class 8 at [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] or [[gps-bandwar-musahri|GPS Bandwar Musahri]], and is one of the ten schools operating in the village.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: UHS +2 Bandwar is the higher secondary school of Bandwar village, established in 1955 as part of Bihar's post-independence expansion of rural education. It holds UDISE code 10201008406 and today offers Classes 9 through 12 with a total enrolment of 601 students — the largest of any school in the village. The school is one of the few government institutions in Bandwar to offer education up to Class 12, and it serves not just Bandwar but also the surrounding panchayats.

content.heading: Enrolment
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school has 315 boys and 286 girls. 394 students are from Other Backward Classes (66%), 99 from Scheduled Castes, and 100 from Muslim families. 524 students — 87% of the school — belong to Below Poverty Line households. This is a striking picture of the village's social fabric, and it reflects the school's role as one of the most inclusive institutions in Bandwar.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school operates from a single pucca block with 8 classrooms, all in good condition. It has 6 toilets each for boys and girls, drinking water, electricity, and internet. It does not, however, have a library, a playground, or a boundary wall. The absence of a library is notable — students preparing for board examinations have no dedicated reading space within the school, and often rely on the [[vaani-vilas-library|Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya]] for their reading needs. The [[sbi-bank|SBI Bandwar branch]] and other village institutions are within a short walk of the school.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 15 teachers — 8 male and 7 female. 14 of them are post-graduates, and 12 hold a B.Ed. or equivalent qualification. The pupil-teacher ratio is roughly 40:1 — above the ideal ratio prescribed by the Right to Education Act, but not unusual for rural secondary schools in Bihar. The school's teaching staff is relatively well-qualified compared to other government schools in the area.

content.heading: Legacy and Challenges
content.text: UHS +2 Bandwar represents both the achievements and the challenges of rural education in Bihar. On the one hand, the school has managed to sustain an enrolment of over 600 students across four classes, and to retain a relatively well-qualified teaching staff. On the other hand, the school has no library, no playground, and no boundary wall — and its pupil-teacher ratio is over 40:1. These are the same challenges that face [[snk-high-school|S.N.K. High School]] and the village's primary schools, and they reflect the wider state of rural education in the region.

faqs.q: What classes does UHS +2 Bandwar offer?
faqs.a: UHS +2 Bandwar offers Classes 9 through 12, making it the only higher secondary school in Bandwar village. It is one of ten schools operating in the village.

faqs.q: How many students study at UHS +2 Bandwar?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 601 students — 315 boys and 286 girls — the largest enrolment of any school in Bandwar. 87% of students belong to Below Poverty Line households.

faqs.q: When was UHS +2 Bandwar established?
faqs.a: UHS +2 Bandwar was established in 1955, as part of Bihar's post-independence expansion of rural education. Its UDISE code is 10201008406.

faqs.q: Does UHS +2 Bandwar have a library?
faqs.a: No — the school does not have a library or a playground. Students often rely on the Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya, the village library on Bandwar Road, for their reading needs.

faqs.q: What is the student-teacher ratio at UHS +2 Bandwar?
faqs.a: The school has 15 teachers for 601 students, giving a pupil-teacher ratio of roughly 40:1 — above the ideal ratio prescribed by the Right to Education Act.

articles.title: MS Bandwar (Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya)
articles.subtitle: The village's government middle school — established 1955
articles.summary: MS Bandwar (Middle School Bandwar) is the government middle school of Bandwar village in Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1955 with UDISE code 10201008401, it serves Classes 1 through 8 with an enrolment of 669 students — one of the largest middle schools in the area. It is managed by the Bihar Department of Education, and functions as the natural bridge between the village's primary schools and [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]].

content.heading: Overview
content.text: MS Bandwar — Rajkiyakrit Madhya Vidyalaya — is the government middle school of Bandwar village. Established in 1955, it serves Classes 1 through 8 and is one of the largest schools in the village, with 669 students on its rolls in the 2025-26 academic year. It is a 'Primary with Upper Primary' school, meaning it educates students from Class 1 all the way to Class 8 — the only school in Bandwar to offer this full range apart from the private [[adharsh-vikash|Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir]] and [[st-paul-school|St. Paul School]].

content.heading: Enrolment and Diversity
content.text: The school has 351 boys and 318 girls. Its enrolment is dominated by Other Backward Classes (506 students, 76%), with 118 Scheduled Caste students and 111 Muslim students. 633 students — 95% — belong to Below Poverty Line households. It is a striking picture of the village's social fabric, and it reflects the school's role as one of the most inclusive institutions in Bandwar. The school's medium of instruction includes Hindi, Sanskrit, and English — a triple-medium approach that is unusual for a government school of this size.

content.heading: Infrastructure
content.text: According to its UDISE+ report, the school runs from 3 pucca building blocks with 8 classrooms. All 8 classrooms, however, need major repair. The boundary wall is pucca but broken. The school does have a library, a playground, electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting — and it received ₹1,00,000 in grants for 2025-26. The combination of a functioning library and a playground is significant — very few government schools in the region have both. The [[vaani-vilas-library|Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya]] on Bandwar Road supplements the school's own library, giving students access to a wider collection.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 17 teachers — 7 male and 10 female. 7 hold B.Ed. qualifications and 7 hold D.El.Ed. diplomas. The pupil-teacher ratio is approximately 39:1. The presence of 10 female teachers in a rural government middle school is notable, and reflects the growing presence of women in Bihar's teaching profession.

content.heading: Bridging Primary and Secondary
content.text: As the only government school in Bandwar offering the full Class 1–8 range, MS Bandwar plays a central role in the village's educational pipeline. Students who complete Class 8 here move on to [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]] or [[snk-high-school|S.N.K. High School]] for their secondary education, or to private alternatives. The school's retention rate and pass percentage at the Class 8 board examination are therefore watched closely by parents across the village.

faqs.q: What classes does MS Bandwar offer?
faqs.a: MS Bandwar offers Classes 1 through 8, making it the only government school in the village to cover the full primary and upper primary range. It serves as the natural bridge to UHS +2 Bandwar and S.N.K. High School.

faqs.q: How many students study at MS Bandwar?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 669 students — 351 boys and 318 girls — one of the largest middle schools in the area. 95% of students belong to Below Poverty Line households.

faqs.q: When was MS Bandwar established?
faqs.a: MS Bandwar was established in 1955, the same year as UHS +2 Bandwar. Its UDISE code is 10201008401.

faqs.q: What is the condition of MS Bandwar's classrooms?
faqs.a: The school runs from 3 pucca building blocks with 8 classrooms. All 8 classrooms, however, need major repair, and the boundary wall is pucca but broken — a common pattern among government schools in rural Bihar.

faqs.q: Does MS Bandwar have a library and playground?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has both a library and a playground, along with electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting. This is unusual for a government school of its size in the region.

articles.title: GPS Paschimibandwar
articles.subtitle: Government primary school in West Bandwar — established 1952
articles.summary: GPS Paschimibandwar (Government Primary School, West Bandwar) is a government primary school in the western part of Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1952 with UDISE code 10201008402, it serves Classes 1 through 5 with 150 students. It is one of the oldest schools in the village, and along with [[gps-mohanpur-kanya|GPS Mohanpur Kanya]] and [[gps-bandwar-musahri|GPS Bandwar Musahri]], forms the backbone of primary education in Bandwar.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: GPS Paschimibandwar is a government primary school in the western part of Bandwar, close to the embankment that runs along the [[burhi-gandak|Burhi Gandak]]. Established in 1952 with UDISE code 10201008402, it is one of the oldest schools in the village — predating even [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]] and [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] by three years. The school's name reflects its location: 'Paschimi' means 'western' in Hindi, and the school serves the families living in the western part of the village.

content.heading: Enrolment
content.text: As per the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 150 students — 83 boys and 67 girls. 118 students are from Other Backward Classes, 27 from Scheduled Castes, and 29 from Muslim families. 126 students — 84% — belong to Below Poverty Line households. The school's enrolment reflects the diversity of West Bandwar, where families from different communities live side by side along the road that leads to the embankment.

content.heading: Infrastructure
content.text: The school operates from 3 pucca building blocks with 7 classrooms — 5 in good condition and 2 in need of major repair. It has a playground, drinking water, electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting. It does not have a library, and the boundary wall is pucca but broken. The presence of a playground is notable — many government primary schools in the region lack this facility, and it makes GPS Paschimibandwar a popular choice for families living nearby.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 9 teachers — 4 male and 5 female. Only 1 holds a B.Ed. qualification, and 5 teachers are below graduate level. The school received ₹30,000 in grants for 2025-26. The relatively low qualification profile of the teaching staff is a common pattern among government primary schools in rural Bihar, and reflects the wider challenges of teacher recruitment and training in the state.

content.heading: Context
content.text: GPS Paschimibandwar is one of three government primary schools in Bandwar — the others being [[gps-mohanpur-kanya|GPS Mohanpur Kanya]] (the girls-only school) and [[gps-bandwar-musahri|GPS Bandwar Musahri]] (the largest primary school, in the Musahri tola). Together, these three schools serve the bulk of the village's primary-age children, and they feed into [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] for upper primary education and [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]] for secondary education.

faqs.q: When was GPS Paschimibandwar established?
faqs.a: GPS Paschimibandwar was established in 1952 — one of the oldest schools in Bandwar village. Its UDISE code is 10201008402, and it serves Classes 1 through 5.

faqs.q: How many students study at GPS Paschimibandwar?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 150 students — 83 boys and 67 girls. 84% of students belong to Below Poverty Line households.

faqs.q: Does GPS Paschimibandwar have a playground?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has a playground, along with drinking water, electricity, internet, and rainwater harvesting. It does not, however, have a library, and its boundary wall is pucca but broken.

faqs.q: Why is the school called 'Paschimibandwar'?
faqs.a: 'Paschimi' means 'western' in Hindi. The school is located in the western part of Bandwar village, close to the embankment along the Burhi Gandak river, and serves families living in that part of the village.

articles.title: GPS Mohanpur Kanya
articles.subtitle: The village's girls-only primary school — established 1956
articles.summary: GPS Mohanpur Kanya is the girls-only government primary school serving Bandwar panchayat in Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1956 with UDISE code 10201009102, it serves Classes 1 through 5 exclusively for girls, with an enrolment of 74 students. It is one of the few dedicated girls' schools in the region, and stands as a quiet counterpoint to the broader gender gap in rural education.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: GPS Mohanpur Kanya is the girls-only government primary school serving the Bandwar panchayat area. Established in 1956 with UDISE code 10201009102, it provides primary education exclusively to girls from Class 1 to Class 5. It is one of the few dedicated girls' schools in the region — most villages in Bihar have only co-educational primary schools, and the survival of a girls-only school into the twenty-first century is notable. Along with [[gps-paschimibandwar|GPS Paschimibandwar]] and [[gps-bandwar-musahri|GPS Bandwar Musahri]], it forms the primary education base for the village, feeding into [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] for upper primary.

content.heading: The School
content.text: According to its UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school has 74 girls on its rolls — 47 from Other Backward Classes, 25 from the general category, and 2 each from Scheduled Caste and Muslim families. 69 of the 74 students — 93% — belong to Below Poverty Line households. The school's relatively small enrolment allows for more individual attention than the village's larger co-educational primary schools.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school runs from a single pucca block with 6 classrooms — 4 in good condition and 2 in need of major repair. It has a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps, but no playground and no boundary wall. Its furniture is minimal, at just 10 units. The presence of a library at a girls' primary school is significant — access to books has historically been a barrier to girls' education in rural Bihar, and the school's library is one of the few in the village.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 8 teachers — 3 male and 5 female. Only 1 holds a B.Ed. qualification and 1 holds a D.El.Ed. diploma. 4 teachers are below graduate level. The school's instructional days for 2025-26 were 236. The presence of 5 female teachers at a girls-only school is significant — girls in rural Bihar often benefit from female teachers as role models and mentors, and the school's staffing reflects this.

content.heading: Girls' Education in Bandwar
content.text: The existence of a dedicated girls' school in Bandwar reflects a broader shift in attitudes towards girls' education in the village. When GPS Mohanpur Kanya was established in 1956, girls' schooling was still uncommon in rural Bihar. Today, girls outnumber boys at several schools in the village — including [[snk-high-school|S.N.K. High School]] (10 of 12 students are girls) and [[nps-kunjartol-wd-9|NPS Kunjartol WD-9]] (175 of 327 students are girls). The girls-only school has played a role in this shift, giving families a space where they could send their daughters with confidence.

faqs.q: Is GPS Mohanpur Kanya a girls-only school?
faqs.a: Yes — GPS Mohanpur Kanya is the girls-only government primary school serving Bandwar panchayat. It provides education exclusively to girls from Class 1 to Class 5, and is one of the few dedicated girls' schools in the region.

faqs.q: When was GPS Mohanpur Kanya established?
faqs.a: GPS Mohanpur Kanya was established in 1956 — a period when girls' schooling was still uncommon in rural Bihar. Its UDISE code is 10201009102.

faqs.q: How many girls study at GPS Mohanpur Kanya?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 74 girls on its rolls. 93% belong to Below Poverty Line households. The school has 8 teachers, 5 of whom are women.

faqs.q: Does GPS Mohanpur Kanya have a library?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has a library, along with drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps. It does not, however, have a playground or a boundary wall.

articles.title: GPS Bandwar Musahri
articles.subtitle: Government primary school in the Musahri tola — established 1995
articles.summary: GPS Bandwar Musahri is a government primary school in the Musahri tola of Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 1995 with UDISE code 10201008403, it serves Classes 1 through 5 with an enrolment of 196 students — the majority from Scheduled Caste and Below Poverty Line households. It is the largest primary school in Bandwar, and one of the ten schools operating in the village.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: GPS Bandwar Musahri is a government primary school in the Musahri tola of Bandwar. Established in 1995 with UDISE code 10201008403, it is the largest primary school in the village, with 196 students on its rolls in the 2025-26 academic year. The school was established relatively late — more than four decades after the village's other primary schools — reflecting the historically lower priority given to education in the Musahri tola. Its founding was part of a broader push in the 1990s to extend primary education to marginalised communities across Bihar.

content.heading: A Mahadalit-Majority School
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, 172 of the school's 196 students — 88% — belong to Scheduled Caste families. 162 students belong to Below Poverty Line households. The presence of a well-enrolled primary school in the Musahri tola reflects the village's commitment to ensuring that education reaches all communities. It also reflects the community's own determination — Musahri families have consistently sent their children to school in large numbers, and the school's enrolment has grown steadily since its founding.

content.heading: Enrolment
content.text: The school has 103 boys and 93 girls — a notable gender balance. Class sizes range from 24 (Class IV) to 68 (Class I). It has 4 classrooms, all in good condition, and 2 functional toilets. The school's relatively small physical footprint — 4 classrooms for 196 students — means that classes are often held in shifts or in shared spaces. Despite this, the school maintains one of the better enrolment ratios in the village.

content.heading: Facilities and Grants
content.text: The school has a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps. It received ₹75,000 in grants for 2025-26. It does not have a playground or a boundary wall. The presence of a library is notable — students in the Musahri tola have limited access to books at home, and the school's library is often their first exposure to a reading culture. Like the [[vaani-vilas-library|Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya]], it plays a role in building the village's literacy base.

content.heading: Context
content.text: GPS Bandwar Musahri is one of three government primary schools in Bandwar — the others being [[gps-paschimibandwar|GPS Paschimibandwar]] and [[gps-mohanpur-kanya|GPS Mohanpur Kanya]]. Together, they serve the bulk of the village's primary-age children. Students from GPS Bandwar Musahri move on to [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] for upper primary education, and then to [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]] or [[snk-high-school|S.N.K. High School]] for secondary education.

faqs.q: When was GPS Bandwar Musahri established?
faqs.a: GPS Bandwar Musahri was established in 1995 — more than four decades after the village's other primary schools. Its UDISE code is 10201008403.

faqs.q: How many students study at GPS Bandwar Musahri?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 196 students — 103 boys and 93 girls — making it the largest primary school in Bandwar. 88% of students belong to Scheduled Caste families.

faqs.q: What is the Musahri tola?
faqs.a: The Musahri tola is a locality within Bandwar village, historically home to families from Scheduled Caste and Mahadalit communities. GPS Bandwar Musahri is the primary school serving this area, established in 1995.

faqs.q: Does GPS Bandwar Musahri have a playground?
faqs.a: No — the school does not have a playground or a boundary wall. It does have a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, ramps, and 2 functional toilets.

articles.title: NPS Kunjartol WD-9
articles.subtitle: Government primary school in Ward 9 — established 2007
articles.summary: NPS Kunjartol WD-9 (New Primary School, Kunjartol Ward 9) is a government primary school in the Kunjartol tola of Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 2007 with UDISE code 10201013301, it serves Classes 1 through 5 with an enrolment of 327 students — the majority from OBC and Muslim families. It is one of the newest schools in the village, and reflects the continuing expansion of primary education in rural Bihar.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: NPS Kunjartol WD-9 is a government primary school in the Kunjartol tola of Bandwar, Ward 9. Established in 2007 with UDISE code 10201013301, it serves Classes 1 through 5 with 327 students — the second-largest primary school in the village. The 'NPS' in its name stands for 'New Primary School', a designation used by the Bihar government for schools established under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan. Its founding in 2007 was part of a wave of new primary schools set up across the state to bring education within reach of every habitation.

content.heading: A Diverse Enrolment
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report card for 2025-26, the school has 152 boys and 175 girls — one of the few schools in Bandwar where girls outnumber boys. 265 students are from Other Backward Classes, 186 from Muslim families, and 60 from Scheduled Castes. 321 students — 98% — belong to Below Poverty Line households, the highest concentration in any Bandwar school. The school's enrolment reflects the diversity of the Kunjartol tola, where OBC, Muslim, and Scheduled Caste families live side by side.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school runs from a single pucca building block with 3 classrooms, all in good condition. It has a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, ramps, and medical checkup facilities — but no playground and no boundary wall. The presence of medical checkup facilities is unusual for a primary school in the region, and reflects the school's participation in the state's school health programme. With 3 classrooms for 327 students, the school operates with a very high classroom density — often running multiple shifts to accommodate all classes.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 14 teachers — 10 male and 4 female. 10 hold D.El.Ed. diplomas, 2 hold B.Ed. qualifications, and 7 are graduates. The pupil-teacher ratio is roughly 23:1 — one of the better ratios among Bandwar's schools. The relatively young teaching staff — many of whom joined after the school's founding in 2007 — reflects the school's recent vintage.

content.heading: Context
content.text: NPS Kunjartol WD-9 is the newest of Bandwar's government primary schools, and its enrolment has grown rapidly since its founding. Along with [[gps-bandwar-musahri|GPS Bandwar Musahri]] (196 students) and [[gps-paschimibandwar|GPS Paschimibandwar]] (150 students), it serves the bulk of the village's primary-age children. Students from NPS Kunjartol move on to [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] for upper primary education. The school's success reflects the broader expansion of primary education in Bihar since the 1990s — a period in which enrolment across the state grew dramatically, especially among girls and marginalised communities.

faqs.q: What does 'NPS' stand for in NPS Kunjartol WD-9?
faqs.a: 'NPS' stands for 'New Primary School' — a designation used by the Bihar government for schools established under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan. NPS Kunjartol WD-9 was established in 2007.

faqs.q: How many students study at NPS Kunjartol WD-9?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 327 students — 152 boys and 175 girls — the second-largest primary school in Bandwar. 98% of students belong to Below Poverty Line households.

faqs.q: Where is NPS Kunjartol WD-9 located?
faqs.a: The school is in the Kunjartol tola of Bandwar village, Ward 9 — one of the newer habitations in the village. It serves families from the surrounding lanes.

faqs.q: Does NPS Kunjartol WD-9 offer medical checkups?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has medical checkup facilities, along with a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and ramps. It does not, however, have a playground or a boundary wall.

articles.title: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir
articles.subtitle: A private primary school in Bandwar — established 2015
articles.summary: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir is a private unaided primary school in Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 2015 with UDISE code 10201008405, it offers Classes 1 through 8 in Hindi medium. It is one of only two private schools in the village, alongside [[st-paul-school|St. Paul School]], and reflects the growing demand for private schooling in rural Bihar.

photos.caption: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir — main building

content.heading: Overview
content.text: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir is a private unaided school in Bandwar, established in 2015 with UDISE code 10201008405. It offers primary education (Classes 1–5) with upper primary classes (6–8), and is one of only two private schools in the village — the other being [[st-paul-school|St. Paul School]]. The school operates from a rented building, and its founding reflects the growing demand for private schooling in rural Bihar — a demand driven by concerns about the quality of government schools and the perceived value of English-medium and 'public school' style education.

content.heading: Why It Matters
content.text: Until 2015, most schools in Bandwar were government-run. The opening of Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir gave parents a private alternative. The school's enrolment of 151 students — 111 from Other Backward Classes, 34 from the general category — reflects the demand for private schooling in rural Bihar. Unlike [[st-paul-school|St. Paul School]], however, Adharsh Vikash has a more mixed enrolment, with 4 Scheduled Caste students and 2 Scheduled Tribe students. Its medium of instruction is Hindi, not English — a distinguishing feature from St. Paul.

content.heading: Facilities
content.text: The school operates from a rented building with 14 classrooms, all in good condition. It has a library, playground, drinking water, electricity, internet, medical checkups, and ramps. Furniture availability, however, is minimal. The presence of a playground and a library at a private school is significant — parents choosing private education often cite these facilities, along with English-medium instruction, as reasons for their choice.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 15 teachers — 7 male and 8 female. 11 of the 15 teachers do not hold a formal teaching qualification (neither B.Ed. nor D.El.Ed.). Only 1 holds a D.El.Ed. diploma. This is a common pattern among low-cost private schools in rural India — teachers are often hired for their subject knowledge rather than formal training, and pay scales are typically lower than in government schools.

content.heading: Context
content.text: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir is one of two private schools in Bandwar, and one of three schools in the village offering the full Class 1–8 range (along with [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] and [[st-paul-school|St. Paul School]]). Its students typically come from families who can afford the fees — the school's enrolment includes 111 OBC students and 34 from the general category, with only a small number from Scheduled Caste and Muslim families. This enrolment profile reflects the wider pattern of private schooling in rural India, where access is often limited by cost.

faqs.q: When was Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir established?
faqs.a: Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir was established in 2015 — one of the first private schools in Bandwar. Its UDISE code is 10201008405.

faqs.q: What classes does Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir offer?
faqs.a: The school offers Classes 1 through 8 — primary with upper primary. It is one of three schools in Bandwar offering the full Class 1–8 range, along with MS Bandwar and St. Paul School.

faqs.q: How many students study at Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 151 students — 84 boys and 67 girls. 111 students are from Other Backward Classes, and 34 from the general category.

faqs.q: Do teachers at Adharsh Vikash have formal teaching qualifications?
faqs.a: Most do not — 11 of the school's 15 teachers hold neither a B.Ed. nor a D.El.Ed. qualification. This is a common pattern among low-cost private schools in rural India.

articles.title: St. Paul School, Bandwar
articles.subtitle: A private English-medium school — established 2015
articles.summary: St. Paul School is a private unaided English-medium school in Bandwar village, Begusarai, Bihar. Established in 2015 with UDISE code 10201008404, it offers Classes 1 through 8 in English and Hindi medium. It serves primarily middle-income families, with only 7% of students from Below Poverty Line households — a striking contrast to the village's government schools, where BPL enrolment ranges from 84% to 98%.

photos.caption: St. Paul School, Bandwar — main building

content.heading: Overview
content.text: St. Paul School is a private unaided English-medium school in Bandwar, established in 2015 with UDISE code 10201008404. It offers Classes 1 through 8 and is one of the only two private schools in the village — the other being [[adharsh-vikash|Adharsh Vikash Vidhya Mandir]]. Unlike Adharsh Vikash, St. Paul School's medium of instruction is primarily English, with Hindi as a secondary language. This English-medium focus is a key reason for the school's popularity among families who see English fluency as an important asset for their children's future.

content.heading: A Different Enrolment
content.text: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, St. Paul School has 209 students — 149 boys and 60 girls. Only 15 students (7%) belong to Below Poverty Line households, compared to 87–98% in the village's government schools. 62 students are from the general category — a much higher proportion than at any government school in Bandwar. This is clearly a school serving Bandwar's middle-income families. The gender ratio is also notable: 149 boys to 60 girls, the highest male-to-female ratio of any school in the village.

content.heading: Infrastructure
content.text: The school has 11 classrooms (8 in good condition), a private pucca building, a library, an ICT lab, drinking water, electricity, internet, medical checkups, and ramps. It does not have a playground. The school received formal recognition for its primary classes in 2017 and for upper primary in 2020. The presence of an ICT lab is notable — very few schools in the region have computer facilities, and this is a significant draw for families choosing private education.

content.heading: Teachers
content.text: The school has 14 teachers — 11 male and 3 female. Only 2 hold B.Ed. qualifications; 5 teachers have no formal teaching qualification. This is consistent with the wider pattern of private unaided schools in rural Bihar. The school's teacher profile reflects its focus on English-medium instruction — teachers are often hired for their English fluency and subject knowledge, rather than formal training.

content.heading: A Contrast With Government Schools
content.text: The differences between St. Paul School and Bandwar's government schools are stark. Where [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] has 95% BPL students, St. Paul has just 7%. Where [[uhs-plus-2-bandwar|UHS +2 Bandwar]] has a pupil-teacher ratio of 40:1, St. Paul's is closer to 15:1. Where most government schools lack libraries, ICT labs, or English-medium instruction, St. Paul has all three. These contrasts reflect the wider stratification of education in rural India — where families who can afford private schooling increasingly choose it, while government schools serve the poorest households.

faqs.q: What is the medium of instruction at St. Paul School?
faqs.a: St. Paul School's medium of instruction is primarily English, with Hindi as a secondary language. This English-medium focus is a key reason for the school's popularity among middle-income families in Bandwar.

faqs.q: When was St. Paul School established?
faqs.a: St. Paul School was established in 2015 — one of the first private schools in Bandwar. It received recognition for its primary classes in 2017 and for upper primary in 2020. Its UDISE code is 10201008404.

faqs.q: How many students study at St. Paul School?
faqs.a: According to the UDISE+ report for 2025-26, the school has 209 students — 149 boys and 60 girls. Only 7% of students belong to Below Poverty Line households, compared to 87–98% in government schools.

faqs.q: Does St. Paul School have an ICT lab?
faqs.a: Yes — the school has an ICT (Information and Communication Technology) lab, along with a library, drinking water, electricity, internet, and medical checkups. It does not, however, have a playground.

articles.title: Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya
articles.subtitle: The village library on Bandwar Road — established 1945
articles.summary: Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya (वाणी विलास पुस्तकालय) is the village library of Bandwar, located on Bandwar Road near the Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar. Established on 5 November 1945, its current building was inaugurated on 5 September 2025 by Rajya Sabha MP Rakesh Sinha. Built with contributions from Muktinath Singh and Girija Singh, the library houses a collection of books in numbered cabinets, along with a reading area decorated with portraits of national leaders. It stands as one of the village's most important public institutions.

Portrait-lined walls and natural light in the reading area.
Commemorative plaques record the library’s foundation and inauguration.
Numbered wooden cabinets preserve the library’s book collection.

content.heading: Overview
content.text: Standing on Bandwar Road near the [[shaheed-dwar|Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar]], the library occupies a single-storey white building with a red iron entrance gate. Inside, numbered wooden cabinets and open bookshelves hold Hindi literature, Bengali works, Islamic texts, and reference material. It adds a dedicated public reading space to the village's educational institutions, complementing the libraries at [[ms-bandwar|MS Bandwar]] and [[gps-mohanpur-kanya|GPS Mohanpur Kanya]].

content.heading: History and Origin
content.text: The library was established on 5 November 1945. Muktinath Singh donated the land for the library building and, together with Girija Singh, supported the initiative for its development. The current building's approximately ₹30 lakh construction cost was supported by ₹15 lakh from the MPLAD fund associated with Rakesh Sinha and ₹15 lakh from Bandwar Gram Panchayat through the Fifteenth Finance Commission allocation. The current building was inaugurated on 5 September 2025, Teachers' Day, reflecting the library's purpose as a space for learning.

content.heading: Services & Facilities
content.text: The library is more than just a reading room. It offers Book Lending (Hindi, Bengali, Islamic texts, reference materials), Free Wi-Fi & Workspace for students and remote workers, Workshops & Classes (from spoken word poetry to digital literacy), Community Events (storytelling evenings, harvest festivals, village council meetings), a Children's Corner with picture books and educational toys, and a unique Seed Library where villagers can borrow seeds, grow gardens, and return seeds at harvest.

content.heading: The Reading Area
content.text: A large wooden table and black metal chairs form the heart of the reading room, seating around a dozen readers. Framed portraits of national leaders, including Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, line the walls. Large windows bring in daylight and views of trees, while ceiling fans keep air moving. Cabinets bear the prefix 'वा.वि.पु.', short for the library's name, followed by a number. The room is especially valued during school examination season.

content.heading: Featured Collection & Events
content.text: The collection includes notable books like 'The Midnight Library' by Matt Haig, 'A Village Called Hope' by Priya Nair, and 'Stories from the Soil' by local authors. The library hosts regular events, including a Summer Reading Challenge (June 1 – August 31) where children compete to read the most books, Storytelling Evenings every 2nd Friday at 6 PM where elders share folk tales, and Art & Craft Workshops teaching traditional rangoli, pottery, and papercraft.

content.heading: Voices from the Village
content.text: The library is deeply cherished by the community. Sunita Devi, a teacher and volunteer, says, 'This library is the soul of our village. My children discovered the joy of reading here.' Retired educator Shyam Prasad calls it his 'second home' where he spends his afternoons reading and mentoring young students. Farmer Ravi Kumar shares, 'The seed library changed my life! I started a small kitchen garden and now supply fresh vegetables to the village market.'

content.heading: Present Day
content.text: Run daily by the वाणी विलास पुस्तकालय committee, the library welcomes students and older residents as an active part of village life. It carries forward the legacy of its late founders, including Ramsharan Sharma, Rajendra Singh, Sachidanand Pathak, and Shri Narayan Pathak. It stands as an expression of the village's commitment to education. You can explore more about the library and its initiatives on their official website: https://vanivilaspushtakalya.netlify.app

faqs.q: When was Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya established?
faqs.a: The library was established on 5 November 1945. However, its current building was inaugurated much later on 5 September 2025.

faqs.q: Who built the current building of Vaani Vilas Pustakalaya?
faqs.a: The land was donated by Muktinath Singh. The construction of the current building cost approximately ₹30 lakh, funded by ₹15 lakh from the MPLAD fund (Rakesh Sinha) and ₹15 lakh from Bandwar Gram Panchayat.

faqs.q: What services does the library offer?
faqs.a: The library offers book lending, free Wi-Fi, workshops, community events, a children's corner, and a unique seed library for farmers. It also hosts a Summer Reading Challenge and monthly storytelling evenings.

faqs.q: Who inaugurated the current building?
faqs.a: The current building was inaugurated by Rajya Sabha MP Rakesh Sinha on 5 September 2025 (Teachers' Day).

faqs.q: Where is the library located?
faqs.a: It is located on Bandwar Road, near the Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar. It is a single-storey white building with a red iron gate. The official website is https://vanivilaspushtakalya.netlify.app.
